sarah_support: FYI - Customer (AcmeApps) opened an escalation: SSE stream cuts off mid-event when routed through their grpc-gateway -> envoy -> our upstream. Client sees partial JSON like `data: {\"id\":42, \"msg\":\"hello` then connection drops and client reconnects. They attached a curl trace and say they were billed for 3 partial responses but only one logical event arrived. :alarm:

maya_eng: Can you paste the exact curl command + request/response headers they used? Two common culprits: intermediary buffering (Cloudflare / LB / Envoy filters) and grpc-web/gRPC->SSE translation mismatches.

sarah_support: Here's the minimal repro they gave (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" --http2 https://proxy.example.com/stream/updates -N
```
And server-side snippet from their proxy logs shows upstream receiving small 40-200 byte chunks, then FINs: `stream: chunked, seen CRLF? yes, frames: 3, last_frame_len: 13, connection: close`

nick_infra: Two quick checks: 1) Are they using grpc-web -> envoy filter or the grpc transcoder? Those can buffer until they think a message boundary is complete. 2) Does the path go through any CDN / L7 that enforces minimum chunk sizes? Cloudflare and some GCP load balancers will buffer small chunks and coalesce/flush oddly.

nick_infra: Repro commands I use locally: `curl --http2 -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" ...` to simulate http2 client, or `nghttp -nv https://...` to inspect frames. Also capture with `tcpdump -i any -s0 -w sse.pcap port 443` then open in Wireshark and look for `:event`, `:data` boundaries.

alex_cust_success: Customer confirmed they have Cloudflare + internal grpc-gateway (which does grpc->http1.1 bridging). They also rotate JWTs every 5m via a token refresh proxy; sometimes the refresh happens mid-stream. Could auth refresh be causing a half-close?

maya_eng: Yes — mid-stream auth rotation can trigger a proxy to send a RST/FIN while the client is still reading, producing truncated messages. Also check for missing trailing CRLFs on the server SSE flush path. Intermediaries often look for CRLF pairs to decide flush boundaries.

deploy-bot: deploy: service/grpc-gateway updated to image grpc-gateway:v2.3.1 by @maya_eng 3h ago

maya_eng: Quick mitigation steps to try (ask customer to try, low risk):
- Ensure server uses `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and does not set `Content-Length` on streaming responses.
- Add header `X-Accel-Buffering: no` (nginx/Envoy/Accel hint) or set `proxy_buffering off` on the proxy in front.
- If using Envoy, disable `grpc_json_transcoder` or test with that filter removed.
- Ensure token refresh happens out-of-band or use token with stream scope so mid-stream rotation won't force reconnect.

maya_eng: Example diagnostic curl to compare http1.1 vs http2 behavior:
```
# HTTP/2 client
curl --http2 -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -N https://proxy.example.com/stream/updates > /tmp/h2.out
# HTTP/1.1 client
curl --http1.1 -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -N https://proxy.example.com/stream/updates > /tmp/h1.out
```
Compare bytes and timing with `hexdump -C` to see chunk boundaries.

sarah_support: Customer will run the two curls and provide pcaps and the h2/h1 outputs. They asked about billing: they were charged for repeated partial responses — is there a pattern we can use to identify and potentially credit?

nick_infra: We should be able to query our usage logs for that customer and correlate `request_id` + `connection_id` for rapid reconnects within a short window. If we see N tiny responses (token counts low) followed by one final, that's evidence. I started a ticket: SUP-3245 and filed initial notes.

maya_eng: Action items:
- sarah_support: get pcaps + h1/h2 curl outputs and the proxy config (Envoy filters + CDN).
- nick_infra: run a reproduce locally with the same envoy config; try toggling grpc-web / transcoder filters and `proxy_buffering` settings.
- I (maya_eng): add a short test harness that streams ~1.5KB events in many small writes to catch coalescing behavior.

sarah_support: Thanks — customer will upload artifacts to the ticket. Marking as P1 for now because of billing and data-loss perception. :white_flag:

nick_infra: I'll ping eng-runtime once we have pcaps. If it's Envoy buffering at the gateway layer we'll prepare a customer-facing note + recommended config changes.

sarah_support: Uploaded files to SUP-3245 (pcap + h1_h2 outputs). I'll drop a link in the ticket thread.

maya_eng: Good. If we confirm intermediary buffering, recommend these long-term fixes: use explicit SSE-friendly route that bypasses grpc JSON filters, add keepalive and larger flushes on server side (send occasional `:\n` comments to keep connection lively), and coordinate token refresh off the stream.

alex_cust_success: I'll follow up on the billing side after we confirm logs.

sarah_support: Closing loop here — thanks all, will wait for eng repro. :pray:
